full_name: Real Club de Golf El Prat, Rosa (Pink) Course

summary.text: The Rosa (Pink) course at Real Club de Golf El Prat is made of the Bosque and Arriba nines of Greg Norman's 45-hole layout near Barcelona.

setting.text: The Bonvilar site is a 220-hectare estate between Terrassa and Sabadell, on the green corridor linking the Sant Llorenc del Munt i l'Obac and Collserola natural parks.
The club has a Biosphere sustainability certification.
Where2golf says the front nine is relatively flat and played in and out of mature pine forest, while the back nine is more open and undulating with panoramic views.
The club lists bentgrass greens of the A4 variety, which it says is the grass used at Augusta.

history.text: The club traces to 1912, when the Count of Churruca founded Barcelona Golf Club, later known as Pedralbes Golf Club.
It became 'Royal' after a visit from King Alfonso XIII.
It was the first golf club in Barcelona.
In 1954 city growth forced a move to a site between El Prat de Llobregat and the sea beside Barcelona airport, and it became Real Club de Golf El Prat.
Barcelona airport's expansion in 1997 forced a second move, to the Bonvilar estate, where Greg Norman designed 45 holes.
The new club was built in 2003, according to the club's history page.
El Prat has hosted the Spanish Open ten times: 1956, 1959, 1963, 1971, 1978, 1981, 1998, 1999, 2011 and 2015.
Seve Ballesteros died on 7 May 2011 while El Prat was hosting the Spanish Open, and winner Thomas Aitken dedicated his victory to him.
In 2015 James Morrison won the Spanish Open at El Prat with a 278, ahead of defending champion Miguel Angel Jimenez.
The inaugural Estrella Damm Catalunya Championship was played there from 7 to 10 May 2026, won by Yurav Premlall by a record 14 shots at 28 under, according to Barcelona Golf.
Greg Norman has said the Pink is his favourite of the three layouts, according to Barcelona Golf.

trivia.text: In top100golfcourses' 2026 ranking of Spain's courses the Pink is eighth.
Barcelona Golf says Golf Digest ranks the Pink among the top ten courses in Spain.
Barcelona Golf counts more than 110 bunkers across the estate.

1.text: A par five with a slight dogleg right, bunkers in two zones, and a narrow green that is long from front to back.

3.text: The shortest par three on the course, with forest around the green.

6.text: A par three with a high, volcano-shaped green ringed by a waste bunker, which the club calls one of the course's most emblematic holes.

8.text: A par four the club calls perhaps the course's most complicated, with forest both sides and a small green guarded by three bunkers.

9.text: A reachable par five with bunkers down the right of the fairway, the last three of which form the letters AGN for 'Architect Greg Norman'.

10.text: A par five with a dogleg right, a riverbed to cross from the elevated tee, and a huge pine in play on the second shot.

12.text: The club says this uphill dogleg-left par four is Greg Norman's preferred hole, with seven bunkers around tee and green.

13.text: A long par three with bunkers lining a long green.

17.text: A tough uphill par four with a semi-blind approach to a fast green, per the club's hole description.

local.text: The club is at Plans de Bonvilar, Terrassa, 26 km from Barcelona.
Barcelona Golf puts the drive from central Barcelona on the C-58 motorway at 25 to 35 minutes.
The clubhouse was designed by Catalan architect Carlos Ferrater, according to Barcelona Golf.
